body_md)\n        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n            return _render_form(\n                request, user, item=item, title=title, slug=slug, body_md=body_md,\n                error=f\"That slug is already used by another {label.lower()}.\",\n            )\n        return RedirectResponse(f\"{url_prefix}?saved={redirect_saved_as}\", status_code=303)\n\n    def _apply_status_change(request, user, item_id, *, new_status, saved_as, csrf_token):\n        if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n            return _render_list(\n                request, user, error=\"Your session expired — please try again.\", status_code=403,\n            )\n        item = content_module.get_content(item_id, kind)\n        if _render_form(request, user, item=None, title=\"\", slug=\"\", body_md=\"\", error=None)\n\n    @router.post(\"/new\")\n    def create_item(\n        request: Request,\n        title: str = _save(request, user, item=None, title=title, slug=slug, body_md=body_md,\n                     redirect_saved_as=\"created\")\n\n    @router.get(\"/{item_id}/edit\")\n    def edit_item_form(request: status_code=303)\n        return _render_form(\n            request, user, item=item, title=item[\"title\"], slug=item[\"slug\"],\n            body_md=item[\"body_md\"], error=None,\n        )\n\n    @router.post(\"/{item_id}/edit\")\n    def update_item(\n        request: Request,\n        item_id: int,\n        title: str = Form(...),\n        slug: str = Form(...),\n        body_md: str = @router.post(\"/{item_id}/delete\")\n    def delete_item(\n        request: Request,\n        item_id: int,\n        csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n        user=Depends(require_editor_or_admin),\n    ):\n        if not security.verify_csrf(csrf_token, request.cookies.get(security.CSRF_COOKIE)):\n            return _render_list(\n                request, user, error=\"Your session expired — please @router.post(\"/{item_id}/publish\")\n    def publish_item(\n        request: Request, item_id: int, csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n        user=Depends(_require_admin_to_publish),\n    ):\n @router.post(\"/{item_id}/unpublish\")\n    def unpublish_item(\n        request: Request, item_id: int, csrf_token: str = Form(...),\n        user=Depends(_require_admin_to_publish),\n    ):\n @router.post(\"/preview\")\n    def preview_item(body_md: str = Form(\"\"), user=Depends(require_editor_or_admin)):\n        \"\"\"Render+sanitize arbitrary Markdown for the live preview pane. {"parentUuid":"7073168a-8517-4788-8380-eebf6a25fc8f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7d8b3a31-fbfb-487a-80a7-397c044958f9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: C:\\Users\\rajan\\.claude\\plugins\\cache\\claude-plugins-official\\mattpocock-skills\\1.2.3\\skills\\engineering\\tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\r\n\r\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\r\n\r\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\r\n\r\n## What a good test is\r\n\r\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\r\n\r\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\r\n\r\n## Seams: where tests go\r\n\r\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\r\n\r\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\r\n\r\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\r\n\r\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\r\n\r\n## Anti-patterns\r\n\r\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\r\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\r\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\r\n\r\n## Rules of the loop\r\n\r\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\r\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\r\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\r\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"fc6e9593-6801-4886-8e8c-9c0a89e06535","timestamp":"2026-10-07T05:14:26.661Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01Ex5xGXQFNEdK1G6f5Nwhwa","session_id":"79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"5e31a13b-376d-4c3f-b0ab-aec3035d9532","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"7d8b3a31-fbfb-487a-80a7-397c044958f9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Km7RyX9WrySk32s7RdktfH","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\r\n\r\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\r\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\r\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\r\n\"\"\"\r\nfrom __future__ import annotations\r\n\r\nimport argparse\r\nimport subprocess\r\nimport sys\r\n\r\nfrom app import settings\r\nfrom app.publish import render_site\r\n\r\n\r\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\r\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\r\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\r\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\r\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\r\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\r\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\r\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\r\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\r\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\r\n\r\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\r\n        import uvicorn\r\n\r\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\r\n        return 0\r\n\r\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\r\n        out = render_site()\r\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\r\n        return 0\r\n\r\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\r\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\r\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\r\n            return 1\r\n        result = subprocess.run(\r\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\r\n             str(settings.SITE)],\r\n        )\r\n        if result.returncode == 0:\r\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\r\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\r\n        return result.returncode\r\n    return 1\r\n\r\n\r\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\r\n    raise SystemExit(main())\r\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nCreates one admin and one editor user (passwords read from .env, never\nhard-coded). As later tickets add Posts/Pages, this script grows to seed\nexample content too.\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\n\nfrom app import settings  # {"parentUuid":"e1906bdf-8e1c-4d53-a73b-2f8f51ced2c5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnJktkTNLSQwLDreAd3N","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Your three answers fix the design. Before I write any tests, I need you to approve where they go, and two smaller design choices.\n\n## T15 design\n\n- **Storage:** a new `revisions` table, one row per saved version: the item, its title, slug and body, who saved it, when, and whether the save was a rollback.\n- **When a revision is recorded:**\n  - when an item is created\n  - on every edit\n  - on every rollback (as a new row, recorded as \"rolled back to version N\")\n  - not on publish or unpublish\n- **Editor screen:** under the form, a \"Revisions\" list, newest first. Each row shows the version number, who saved it, when, and the title. A collapsible part shows that version's Markdown. The newest row is marked **Current**; every other row gets a **Roll back** button, which is a POST with a CSRF token. Editors and Admins can both use it.\n- **Rollback reuses the editor's save path**, so it gets the same slug checks for free. If the old slug is now taken, you see the editor with \"That slug is already used by another post\", and nothing changes.\n- **Delete:** deleting an item also deletes its revisions.\n\n## Design choice A: how your existing `cms.db` gets the new table\n\nRight now the schema is only created when the seed script runs. So the app would crash on the new table until you re-seed.\n\nMy fix: `db.connect()` brings the database up to date the first time it opens each file. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is safe to run more than once, so this works on old and new databases alike. It runs once per process.\n\n## Design choice B: items saved before T15\n\nItems in your database from before T15 have no revisions. The first edit after T15 would overwrite them with no way back.\n\nMy fix: that same update step gives each such item one starting revision, using its current text, its author, and its last-updated time. That way their pre-T15 version can be rolled back to.\n\n## Test seams to approve\n\n1. **The admin web pages (the main seam).** I'll drive them through the logged-in test client, the same way `tests/test_posts.py` does, and check results with `content.get_content` plus the edit page itself:\n   - saving creates a revision that shows on the edit page\n   - rollback brings back the old title, slug and body, and adds a \"rolled back\" revision\n   - a slug conflict during rollback shows the error and changes nothing\n   - an Editor can roll back\n   - a revision id that belongs to a *different* item is refused (so nobody can copy one item's text into another)\n2. **Updating an existing database.** Build a pre-T15 database by hand (no `revisions` table, one item already in it), open it, and check that the table now exists and the item has its one starting revision.\n3. **Adding to the existing safety tests** (no new seams): the rollback route goes into the access-control and CSRF sweep, and the edit screen with revisions goes into the phone-width and link tests.\n\nI'll use Posts for the behaviour tests. Pages go through the same `build_content_router`, so one Pages test should be enough to show both are wired up.\n\nIf you're happy with A, B and the seams, I'll create the T15 issue (labelled `stretch`) and start on the first failing test.\n\nTwo things only you can do (both still pending):\n- **Push `d4d5b4a`.** `main` is still one commit ahead of GitHub. Run `! git push`, or tell me to push it.\n- **Set the phase file:** `! echo T15 > .claude/state/phase`"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2345,"cache_read_input_tokens":71896,"output_tokens":1322,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":210},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2345,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1322,"cache_read_input_tokens":71896,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2345,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2345},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"be37f27e-3478-4cf9-98b4-8c421c522d03","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfnJktULXZxvaQmqeadVN","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:tdd","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"8c407a4f-4deb-4eff-8f58-bb0b2f0bce63","timestamp":"2026-10-07T05:15:13.960Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms","sessionId":"79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"beb8c6dc-f6fe-4273-95f0-306d458ed3cb","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnKENEwrVwKwzFKhHako","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01QDEyBHCiuS4C5kSjUTRT1a","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1\\scratchpad\\t15-issue.md","content":"## Parent\n\nSpec: #1 (stretch goal named in \"Out of Scope\" / \"Further Notes\")\n\n## What to build\n\nRevision history with rollback for Posts and Pages. Every save of a content item's title, slug and body is kept as a **Revision**, with who saved it and when, so an Editor or Admin can see earlier versions and roll the item back to one.\n\n- A revision is recorded when an item is created, on every edit, and on every rollback. Publish and unpublish change status, not content, so they record no revision.\n- The editor screen lists the item's revisions, newest first: version number, who saved it, when, and the title, with the saved Markdown viewable. The newest is marked **Current**; every other has a **Roll back** button.\n- Rolling back is a state-changing POST with a CSRF token, open to Editors and Admins (Editors can already edit and delete any item). It goes through the same save path as the editor, so the same slug checks apply, and it is itself recorded as a new revision (\"rolled back to version N\").\n- Deleting an item deletes its revisions.\n- Existing databases are brought up to date when they are first opened: the `revisions` table is created if missing, and each item saved before this ticket gets one starting revision from its current state, so its pre-T15 version can be rolled back to.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Creating, editing, and rolling back a Post or Page each record a revision with title, slug, body, who and when\n- [ ] The edit screen lists revisions newest first, marks the current one, and offers Roll back on the others\n- [ ] Rolling back restores the old title, slug and body and records a new revision noting the rollback\n- [ ] Rolling back to a slug now used by another item of the same kind shows the editor's \"slug already used\" error and changes nothing\n- [ ] Editors and Admins can roll back; anonymous visitors are redirected to log in\n- [ ] A revision id belonging to a different item is refused (no cross-item restore)\n- [ ] The rollback route rejects a forged CSRF token and is part of the access-control sweep\n- [ ] A database created before this ticket gains the `revisions` table and a starting revision per existing item, with no re-seed\n- [ ] The edit screen with revisions fits a 390px phone and every link on it stays relative and resolves\n- [ ] `CONTEXT.md` defines Revision and Roll back\n- [ ] The full test suite passes\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #15 (T14: Friendlier visual design for the admin console and public site)\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":589,"cache_read_input_tokens":77163,"output_tokens":1491,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":250},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":589,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1491,"cache_read_input_tokens":77163,"cache_creation_input_tokens":589,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":589},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01QDEyBHCiuS4C5kSjUTRT1a":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1\\scratchpad\\t15-issue.md","content":"## Parent\n\nSpec: #1 (stretch goal named in \"Out of Scope\" / \"Further Notes\")\n\n## What to build\n\nRevision history with rollback for Posts and Pages. Every save of a content item's title, slug and body is kept as a **Revision**, with who saved it and when, so an Editor or Admin can see earlier versions and roll the item back to one.\n\n- A revision is recorded when an item is created, on every edit, and on every rollback. Publish and unpublish change status, not content, so they record no revision.\n- The editor screen lists the item's revisions, newest first: version number, who saved it, when, and the title, with the saved Markdown viewable. The newest is marked **Current**; every other has a **Roll back** button.\n- Rolling back is a state-changing POST with a CSRF token, open to Editors and Admins (Editors can already edit and delete any item). {"parentUuid":"7bf2cd8e-b8cd-497f-8d75-2a2c3b29e6f2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnKHrsxjpt7n4HyAVzTL","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011KLva4R2V52EQ9wtQdah6D","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\content.py","old_string":"def create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","new_string":"def _record_revision(conn: sqlite3.Connection, content_id: int, title: str, slug: str,\n                     body_md: str, saved_by: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot one save as the item's next version, inside the caller's\n    transaction so the content row and its revision commit together.\"\"\"\n    conn.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO revisions (content_id, version, title, slug, body_md, saved_by) \"\n        \"SELECT ?, COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1, ?, ?, ?, ? \"\n        \"FROM revisions WHERE content_id = ?\",\n        (content_id, title, slug, body_md, saved_by, content_id),\n    )\n\n\ndef create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        _record_revision(conn, cur.lastrowid, title, slug, body_md, author_id)\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str,\n                   *, editor_id: int) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        if cur.rowcount:\n            _record_revision(conn, content_id, title, slug, body_md, editor_id)\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_revisions(content_id: int, kind: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"An item's revisions, newest first, with who saved each one.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT revisions.*, users.email AS saved_by_email FROM revisions \"\n            \"JOIN content ON content.id = revisions.content_id \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = revisions.saved_by \"\n            \"WHERE revisions.content_id = ? AND content.kind = ? \"\n            \"ORDER BY revisions.version DESC\",\n            (content_id, kind),\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1209,"cache_read_input_tokens":82900,"output_tokens":1842,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":40},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1209,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1842,"cache_read_input_tokens":82900,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1209,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1209},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_011KLva4R2V52EQ9wtQdah6D":{"file_path":"C:\\Rajan\\E disk\\My work\\IPHS400\\code\\mp2-cms\\app\\content.py","old_string":"def create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? No ORM (see spec Implementation Decisions).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS content (\n    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('post', 'page')),\n    title TEXT NOT NULL,\n    slug TEXT NOT NULL,\n    body_md TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')) DEFAULT 'draft',\n    author_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    UNIQUE (kind, slug)\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef connect(db_path: Path | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    \"\"\"Open a connection to the CMS database, reading the current path lazily\n    (settings.DATABASE_PATH) so tests can monkeypatch it per-test.\"\"\"\n    path = db_path if db_path is not None else settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    return conn\n\n\ndef init_db(db_path: Path | None = None) -> None:\n    conn = connect(db_path)\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":28,"oldLines":6,"newStart":28,"newLines":22,"lines":["     updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),","     UNIQUE (kind, slug)"," );","+","+-- One row per saved version of a content item (see CONTEXT.md: Revision).","+-- `version` counts 1, 2, 3... within one item; AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","newString":"def _record_revision(conn: sqlite3.Connection, content_id: int, title: str, slug: str,\n                     body_md: str, saved_by: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Snapshot one save as the item's next version, inside the caller's\n    transaction so the content row and its revision commit together.\"\"\"\n    conn.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO revisions (content_id, version, title, slug, body_md, saved_by) \"\n        \"SELECT ?, COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1, ?, ?, ?, ? \"\n        \"FROM revisions WHERE content_id = ?\",\n        (content_id, title, slug, body_md, saved_by, content_id),\n    )\n\n\ndef create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        _record_revision(conn, cur.lastrowid, title, slug, body_md, author_id)\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str,\n                   *, editor_id: int) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        if cur.rowcount:\n            _record_revision(conn, content_id, title, slug, body_md, editor_id)\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_revisions(content_id: int, kind: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"An item's revisions, newest first, with who saved each one.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT revisions.*, users.email AS saved_by_email FROM revisions \"\n            \"JOIN content ON content.id = revisions.content_id \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = revisions.saved_by \"\n            \"WHERE revisions.content_id = ? AND content.kind = ? \"\n            \"ORDER BY revisions.version DESC\",\n            (content_id, kind),\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()","originalFile":"\"\"\"Content (Posts and Pages) data access. No ORM (see spec Implementation\nDecisions). Posts and Pages share this one table and these functions,\ndistinguished only by `kind` ('post' | 'page') — see CONTEXT.md.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom app import db as db_module\n\nSLUG_RE = re.compile(r\"^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$\")\n\nSTATUS_DRAFT = \"draft\"\nSTATUS_PUBLISHED = \"published\"\n\n# A Page is exported to site/<slug>.html, so these slugs would overwrite a\n# file the export itself writes. Maps kind -> {slug: what it would clobber}.\nRESERVED_SLUGS = {\"page\": {\"index\": \"the site's home page\"}}\n\n\ndef reserved_slug_reason(kind: str, slug: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"What `slug` is reserved for within `kind`, or None if it's free.\"\"\"\n    return RESERVED_SLUGS.get(kind, {}).get(slug)\n\n\ndef normalize_slug(raw: str) -> str:\n    return raw.strip().lower()\n\n\ndef validate_slug(raw: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Normalize `raw` and return it if it's a valid slug, else None.\"\"\"\n    normalized = normalize_slug(raw)\n    return normalized if SLUG_RE.match(normalized) else None\n\n\ndef list_content(kind: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT content.*, users.email AS author_email FROM content \"\n            \"JOIN users ON users.id = content.author_id \"\n            \"WHERE content.kind = ? ORDER BY content.created_at DESC\",\n            (kind,),\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef list_published(kind: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM content WHERE kind = ? AND status = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC\",\n            (kind, STATUS_PUBLISHED),\n        ).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef count_by_status() -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Combined draft/published counts across both kinds (Posts and Pages\n    together) — the dashboard shows one total, not split by type.\"\"\"\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        rows = conn.execute(\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM content GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n    counts = {STATUS_DRAFT: 0, STATUS_PUBLISHED: 0}\n    for row in rows:\n        counts[row[\"status\"]] = row[\"n\"]\n    return counts\n\n\ndef list_filtered(*, status: str | None = None, kind: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"All content (Posts and Pages together), optionally narrowed by\n    status and/or kind. None means \"no filter\" (show all) for that axis.\"\"\"\n    query = (\n        \"SELECT content.*, users.email AS author_email FROM content \"\n        \"JOIN users ON users.id = content.author_id WHERE 1 = 1\"\n    )\n    params: list[str] = []\n    if status is not None:\n        query += \" AND content.status = ?\"\n        params.append(status)\n    if kind is not None:\n        query += \" AND content.kind = ?\"\n        params.append(kind)\n    query += \" ORDER BY content.created_at DESC\"\n\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(query, params).fetchall()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_published_by_slug(kind: str, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM content WHERE kind = ? AND slug = ? AND status = ?\",\n            (kind, slug, STATUS_PUBLISHED),\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef get_content(content_id: int, kind: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM content WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\", (content_id, kind)\n        ).fetchone()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO content (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n        return cur.lastrowid\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"\n            \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (title, slug, body_md, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef set_status(content_id: int, kind: str, status: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE content SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') \"\n            \"WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\",\n            (status, content_id, kind),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef delete_content(content_id: int, kind: str) -> None:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM content WHERE id = ? AND kind = ?\", (content_id, kind))\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":116,"oldLines":6,"newStart":116,"newLines":18,"lines":["         conn.close()"," "," ","+def _record_revision(conn: sqlite3.Connection, content_id: int, title: str, slug: str,","+                     body_md: str, saved_by: int) -> None:","+    \"\"\"Snapshot one save as the item's next version, inside the caller's","+    transaction so the content row and its revision commit together.\"\"\"","+    conn.execute(","+        \"INSERT INTO revisions (content_id, version, title, slug, body_md, saved_by) \"","+        \"SELECT ?, COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1, ?, ?, ?, ? \"","+        \"FROM revisions WHERE content_id = ?\",","+        (content_id, title, slug, body_md, saved_by, content_id),","+    )","+","+"," def create_content(kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str, author_id: int) -> int:","     conn = db_module.connect()","     try:"]},{"oldStart":124,"oldLines":25,"newStart":136,"newLines":45,"lines":["             \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",","             (kind, title, slug, body_md, author_id),","         )","+        _record_revision(conn, cur.lastrowid, title, slug, body_md, author_id)","         conn.commit()","         return cur.lastrowid","     finally:","         conn.close()"," "," ","-def update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str) -> None:","+def update_content(content_id: int, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str,","+                   *, editor_id: int) -> None:","     conn = db_module.connect()","     try:","-        conn.execute(","+        cur = conn.execute(","             \"UPDATE content SET title = ?, slug = ?, body_md = ?, \"","             \"updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ? Measured in a real browser: the page fits when the\ndocument is no wider than the viewport. The content is deliberately awkward --\na long unbroken title, a long URL, a wide code block -- because that's what\nreal posts contain and what pushes a narrow layout sideways.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import content as content_module\nfrom app import db as db_module\nfrom tests.conftest import log_in\n\nLONG_WORD = \"Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious-and-then-some-more-words-joined\"\nWIDE_BODY = (\n    \"See https://example.org/a/very/long/path/that/never/breaks/on/its/own/at/all.html\\n\\n\"\n    \"```\\n\" + \"print('a line of code far wider than any phone screen') \" * 3 + \"\\n```\\n\\n\"\n    \"| Column one | Column two | Column three | Column four | Column five |\\n\"\n    \"|---|---|---|---|---|\\n\"\n    \"| some cell text | some cell text | some cell text | some cell text | some cell text |\\n\"\n)\n\n\ndef _admin_id() -> int:\n    conn = db_module.connect()\n    try:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'admin@example.test'\").fetchone()[\"id\"]\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef awkward_content():\n    \"\"\"A published Post and Page whose title and body are hard to fit, each\n    saved twice so its edit screen lists a revision with a Roll back button.\"\"\"\n    author = _admin_id()\n    ids = {}\n    for kind in (\"post\", \"page\"):\n        ids[kind] = content_module.create_content(\n            kind, f\"{kind.title()} {LONG_WORD}\", f\"wide-{kind}\", WIDE_BODY, author)\n        content_module.update_content(\n            ids[kind], kind, f\"{kind.title()} {LONG_WORD}\", f\"wide-{kind}\", WIDE_BODY + \"\nMore.\",\n            editor_id=author)\n        content_module.set_status(ids[kind], kind, content_module.STATUS_PUBLISHED)\n    return ids\n\n\ndef assert_fits_phone(page) -> None:\n    overflow = page.evaluate(\n        \"document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth\")\n    assert overflow <= 0, f\"{page.url} is {overflow}px wider than a 390px phone\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/\", \"/posts/wide-post.html\", \"/wide-page.html\"])\ndef test_public_pages_fit_a_phone(phone, awkward_content, path):\n    phone.goto(path)\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n\n\ndef test_login_page_fits_a_phone(phone):\n    phone.goto(\"/login\")\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n\n\ndef test_login_page_with_its_error_message_fits_a_phone(phone):\n    phone.goto(\"/login\")\n    phone.fill(\"input[name=email]\", \"admin@example.test\")\n    phone.fill(\"input[name=password]\", \"not-the-password\")\n    phone.click(\"button[type=submit]\")\n    phone.wait_for_selector(\".error\", timeout=5000)\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n\n\nADMIN_SCREENS = [\n    \"/admin\", \"/admin/content\", \"/admin/content?status=published&type=post\",\n    \"/admin/posts\", \"/admin/posts/new\", \"/admin/posts/{post}/edit\",\n    \"/admin/pages\", \"/admin/pages/new\", \"/admin/pages/{page}/edit\",\n    \"/admin/users\", \"/admin/users/new\",\n]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", ADMIN_SCREENS)\ndef test_admin_screens_fit_a_phone(phone, awkward_content, path):\n    log_in(phone, \"admin\")\n    phone.goto(path.format(**awkward_content))\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n\n\ndef test_editor_denied_page_fits_a_phone(phone):\n    log_in(phone, \"editor\")\n    response = phone.goto(\"/admin/users\")\n    assert response.status == 403\n    assert_fits_phone(phone)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":41,"oldLines":9,"newStart":41,"newLines":8,"lines":["         ids[kind] Status is unchanged: a Published item's restored text reaches the site on the next static export.\n_Avoid_: restore, revert, undo","originalFile":"# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS: a local admin console where Editors and Admins manage content, and a static public site that publishes it. The content model is intentionally generic — built with no specific client in mind. (A specific client site will be built *using* this CMS as a later, separate project.)\n\n## Roles\n\n**Admin**:\nA CMS user role with full permissions: everything an Editor can do, plus publishing/unpublishing content and managing user accounts (create, change role, deactivate).\n_Avoid_: superadmin, owner\n\n**Editor**:\nA CMS user role that can create, edit, and delete any Post or Page — including another user's drafts — but cannot publish/unpublish content or manage user accounts.\n_Avoid_: contributor, author (an Author is a content attribute, not a role)\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**:\nA dated, feed-like content item with a title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, and timestamps. Appears in the site's chronological feed.\n_Avoid_: article, entry\n\n**Page**:\nA static, evergreen content item — same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public site's navigation once published.\n_Avoid_: static page (redundant)\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe identifier for a Post or Page, unique within its kind, used to build its published path.\n\n**Status (Draft / Published)**:\nThe two states a Post or Page can be in. A Draft is visible only in the admin console; only a Published item reaches the static export.\n_Avoid_: live/unlive, active/inactive\n\n**Author**:\nThe user (Admin or Editor) recorded as having written a given Post or Page. Distinct from whoever most recently edited it.\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Publish** (verb):\nThe admin-only action that flips a content item's status from Draft to Published, making it eligible to appear in the next static export.\n_Avoid_: approve (there's no separate approval workflow — publish is a single, direct action)\n\n**Static export**:\nThe `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages.\n\n**Revision history** _(stretch goal)_:\nA record of a Post or Page's prior saved versions, with the ability to roll back to one.\n\n**Scheduled publishing** _(stretch goal)_:\nSetting a future date/time at which a Draft automatically becomes Published, with no manual step at that time.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":41,"oldLines":8,"newStart":41,"newLines":16,"lines":[" **Static export**:"," The `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages."," ","+**Revision**:","+One saved version of a Post or Page: its title, slug, and body, who saved it, and when, numbered 1, 2, 3… within that item. Every create, edit, and Roll back records one; Publish and unpublish do not, since they change Status, not content.","+_Avoid_: snapshot, history entry","+"," **Revision history** _(stretch goal)_:","-A record of a Post or Page's prior saved versions, with the ability to roll back to one.","+The list of an item's Revisions, newest first, on its edit screen. Two rules bind it:\r\n\r\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\r\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\r\n\r\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\r\n\r\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\r\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\r\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\r\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\r\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\r\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\r\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\r\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\r\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\r\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\r\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\r\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\r\n\r\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\r\n\r\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\r\n\r\n- The full diff command and commit list.\r\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\r\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\r\n\r\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\r\n\r\n- The diff command and commit list.\r\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\r\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\r\n\r\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\r\n\r\n### 5. Aggregate\r\n\r\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\r\n\r\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). When a review surfaces something genuinely unrelated to the current ticket (e.g. a missing nav link from an earlier closed ticket, or a shared helper worth extracting across already-committed files), it's fine to fix it in the same commit as long as it's small, safe, and explicitly disclosed in the commit message/review comment as a deliberate aside rather than hidden in an unrelated diff.\n\nAlways stage files explicitly (`git add <specific paths>`), never `-A`/`.`, and check `git status` before every stage — this project had the user's own in-progress, uncommitted work (an AI Use Statement draft in README.md) sitting in the tree for several tickets in a row; The report follows:\n  **Standards review, T15 (uncommitted diff against d4d5b4a)**\n  \n  **Hard violations (documented standard)**\n  1. `app/content.py` `_record_revision` docstring says \"Snapshot one save…\". CONTEXT.md, Revision: \"_Avoid_: snapshot\". CLAUDE.md requires CONTEXT vocabulary. Suggested fix: \"Record one save as the item's next Revision\".\n  2. `update_content(..., *, editor_id: int, ...)`. CONTEXT.md defines Editor as a role, but an Admin's save also passes through `editor_id`. The column is `saved_by`, so the parameter should use that name too. Borderline: the \"restored\" / \"restores\" wording in the `db.py` comment and the `update_content` and `_save` docstrings. CONTEXT lists \"restore\" under _Avoid_ but uses \"Restoring\" in its own definition, so either the glossary or the code should change.\n  \n  Checked and clean: the rollback form carries a CSRF token and uses a relative `{{ to_root }}` action. Revision title and body are autoescaped (Jinja2Templates autoescapes .html). The content row and its revision commit in one transaction, and an IntegrityError rolls both back on close. `delete_content` is scoped by kind via `rowcount`. The access-control sweep and forged-CSRF lists include both rollback routes. No new dependency.\n  \n  **Correctness risks (judgement)**\n  - `db.connect` leaks the connection: if `_upgrade` raises, `conn` is never closed. The key also never gets cached, so every later `connect()` leaks again. Wrap it in try/except, close, then re-raise.\n  - `init_db` is now `connect(db_path).close()`, so it is a no-op for any path already cached. If the file is deleted and `init_db` runs again in the same process, the schema is not recreated. Also, `Path.resolve()` now runs on every connect.\n  - `seed.py` `_seed_content` inserts content without a revision. It relies on the backfill at the next process start. If a server is already running while seeding happens, seeded items have no revision 1, and their seeded text is lost from history on the first edit. The `BACKFILL_REVISIONS` comment (\"create_content records one\") overlooks this path.\n  - The backfill sets `saved_by = author_id`. CONTEXT says the Author is distinct from the last editor, so backfilled attribution may be wrong.\n  - `tests/test_revisions.py` `_create_post` returns `list_content(\"post\")[0]`, which sorts on `created_at` with one-second resolution. Two tests create several posts per test, and a same-second tie could return the wrong id. That makes these tests potentially flaky.\n  \n  **Baseline smells (judgement)**\n  - Divergent Change: `connect()` now both opens connections and migrates the schema.\n  - Middle Man: `_upgrade` (2 lines, one caller) and `init_db`.\n  - Duplicated Code: `roll_back_item` is a third copy of the \"get_content → 303 → verify_csrf → _csrf_error\" preamble from `update_item` and `create_item`. `get_revision` and `list_revisions` repeat the same kind-scoping `JOIN content`.\n  - Data Clumps: `title, slug, body_md` travel together through `_record_revision` (7 positional params), `update_content`, `_save` and the revision rows.\n  - Repeated Switches / Primitive Obsession: `saved == \"rolled-back\"` adds another branch to the string if-cascade in `content_list.html`. This follows the existing pattern.\n  - Glossary drift: CONTEXT still marks \"Revision history\" as _(stretch goal)_ although it is now implemented.\n</agent-message>"}

Path, admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> None:\n    db_module.init_db(db_path)\n    conn = db_module.connect(db_path)\n    try:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (email, password_hash, role, active) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, 'admin', 1)\",\n            (DEMO_EMAILS[\"admin\"], hash_password(admin_password)),\n        )\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (email, password_hash, role, active) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, 'editor', 1)\",\n            (DEMO_EMAILS[\"editor\"], hash_password(editor_password)),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef _seed_content(\n    db_path: Path, *, kind: str, title: str, slug: str, body_md: str,\n    status: str, author_email: str,\n) -> status, author[\"id\"]),\n        )\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef seed_posts(db_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Seed one published and one draft Post, authored by The newest is the Current one.\n\n**Roll back** (verb):\nRestoring an item's title, slug, and body from an earlier Revision.","newString":"**Revision history**:\nThe list of an item's Revisions, newest first, on its edit screen. The newest is the Current one.\n\n**Roll back** (verb):\nReturning an item's title, slug, and body to those of an earlier Revision.","originalFile":"# CONTEXT.md glossary\n\nA small, WordPress-style web CMS: a local admin console where Editors and Admins manage content, and a static public site that publishes it. The content model is intentionally generic — built with no specific client in mind. (A specific client site will be built *using* this CMS as a later, separate project.)\n\n## Roles\n\n**Admin**:\nA CMS user role with full permissions: everything an Editor can do, plus publishing/unpublishing content and managing user accounts (create, change role, deactivate).\n_Avoid_: superadmin, owner\n\n**Editor**:\nA CMS user role that can create, edit, and delete any Post or Page — including another user's drafts — but cannot publish/unpublish content or manage user accounts.\n_Avoid_: contributor, author (an Author is a content attribute, not a role)\n\n## Content\n\n**Post**:\nA dated, feed-like content item with a title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, and timestamps. Appears in the site's chronological feed.\n_Avoid_: article, entry\n\n**Page**:\nA static, evergreen content item — same fields and operations as a Post, plus appearing in the public site's navigation once published.\n_Avoid_: static page (redundant)\n\n**Slug**:\nThe URL-safe identifier for a Post or Page, unique within its kind, used to build its published path.\n\n**Status (Draft / Published)**:\nThe two states a Post or Page can be in. A Draft is visible only in the admin console; only a Published item reaches the static export.\n_Avoid_: live/unlive, active/inactive\n\n**Author**:\nThe user (Admin or Editor) recorded as having written a given Post or Page. Distinct from whoever most recently edited it.\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Publish** (verb):\nThe admin-only action that flips a content item's status from Draft to Published, making it eligible to appear in the next static export.\n_Avoid_: approve (there's no separate approval workflow — publish is a single, direct action)\n\n**Static export**:\nThe `site/` directory `cms publish` generates from currently-published content only; what `cms deploy` pushes to GitHub Pages.\n\n**Revision**:\nOne saved version of a Post or Page: its title, slug, and body, who saved it, and when, numbered 1, 2, 3… within that item. Every create, edit, and Roll back records one; Publish and unpublish do not, since they change Status, not content.\n_Avoid_: snapshot, history entry\n\n**Revision history** _(stretch goal)_:\nThe list of an item's Revisions, newest first, on its edit screen. The newest is the Current one.\n\n**Roll back** (verb):\nRestoring an item's title, slug, and body from an earlier Revision. Editors and Admins can do it; it is itself recorded as a new Revision, so a Roll back can be undone the same way. Status is unchanged: a Published item's restored text reaches the site on the next static export.\n_Avoid_: restore, revert, undo\n\n**Scheduled publishing** _(stretch goal)_:\nSetting a future date/time at which a Draft automatically becomes Published, with no manual step at that time.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":45,"oldLines":11,"newStart":45,"newLines":11,"lines":[" One saved version of a Post or Page: its title, slug, and body, who saved it, and when, numbered 1, 2, 3… within that item. The **Spec** axis checked each acceptance criterion against the screenshots and the code, and looked for regressions in rubric C5/F2–F4.\n- **Hard rules are clean:** no root-absolute paths (including `url(/…)` in CSS); every POST form still carries its `csrf_token`; field names, actions and methods are unchanged.\n- **Robustness is clean:** `app/style.css` ships with the package (hatch includes non-.py files), and `request.url.path` exists in every admin render, including the access-denied handler and failed-POST re-renders.\n- **Contrast passes WCAG AA** in both themes (tightest: the Draft badge at about 4.7:1).\n- The spec axis rated 7 of 8 criteria met and \"no regressions\" mostly met, pending a full-suite run; that run now passes (see Verification).\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Standards | Focus was a faint box-shadow ring with `outline: none`, so it vanished in Windows forced-colors mode. | A real `outline: 2px solid var(--accent)` with an offset. {"parentUuid":"d7eeb5cb-828e-4e2b-87f3-d768d6195394","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnLGsmsfRTXX6f8vPPdj","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_015q3RbzzWqTkw7NLqWNZ8o1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1\\scratchpad\\t15-review.md","content":"## /code-review findings — T15\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel. The **Standards** axis checked the CLAUDE.md rules, the CONTEXT.md vocabulary, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md and the Fowler smell baseline. The **Spec** axis mapped each acceptance criterion in this issue to the code and the tests.\n\n- **Hard rules are clean.** The Roll back form carries a `csrf_token`, and its action is relative (`{{ to_root }}…`). Revision titles and Markdown are autoescaped by Jinja. No new dependency was added. Drafts still never reach `site/`: export reads `content`, never `revisions`.\n- **Atomicity is clean.** The content row and its revision commit in one transaction. A duplicate-slug `IntegrityError` rolls both back.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance criterion is implemented. Six were fully covered by tests; the gaps the axis found were in assertions, not in behaviour (fixed below).\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Standards | `_record_revision`'s docstring said \"Snapshot\", a word CONTEXT.md lists under *Avoid*. | It now says \"Record one save as the item's next Revision\". |\n| 2 | Standards | `update_content(..., editor_id=)` used a role name (Editor) for a value that can be an Admin. | Renamed to `saved_by`, matching the column. |\n| 3 | Standards | Comments said a Roll back \"restores\", and CONTEXT.md's own definition began with \"Restoring\", although it lists \"restore\" under *Avoid*. | Comments say \"rolls back to\" / \"returns to\"; the glossary now says \"Returning an item's title, slug, and body to those of an earlier Revision\". |\n| 4 | Standards | `db.connect()` leaked the connection if the schema upgrade raised, and leaked again on every later call. | The upgrade now lives in `init_db`, which closes its own connection in `finally`. `connect()` opens its connection only after that succeeds. The two-line `_upgrade` middle man is gone. |\n| 5 | Standards | `init_db` became a no-op for a database file already seen by the process. | `init_db` always runs the schema and backfill. Only `connect()` skips it once a file is known. |\n| 6 | Standards | `app/seed.py` inserts content directly, so seeded items got no version 1 until the next process start. If the server was already running, the seeded text was lost from history on the first edit. | `_seed_content` runs the backfill in the same transaction. New test `test_seeded_demo_content_starts_with_a_first_revision` fails without the fix and passes with it. |\n| 7 | Standards | The tests' `_create_post` took `list_content(...)[0]`, which ties on `created_at` (1-second resolution) when two posts are made in the same second. That could make tests flaky. | It looks the post up by its slug. |\n| 8 | Spec | Criterion 1: nothing asserted \"who and when\" beyond the email, or who saved a Roll back. | Asserts a `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC` timestamp, and that an Admin's Roll back of an Editor's post is recorded under the Admin. |\n| 9 | Spec | Criterion 2: nothing asserted that the Markdown is viewable, or that Roll back appears only on earlier versions. | Both are asserted. |\n| 10 | Spec | Criterion 4: the slug-conflict test didn't assert the status code. | Asserts 200 (the editor is re-rendered with the error). |\n| 11 | Spec | Criterion 9: a *failed* Roll back POST, which renders at the deeper `/revisions/1/rollback` URL, wasn't in the link-resolution test. | Added to `FAILED_POST_PAGES`. |\n| 12 | Standards | CONTEXT.md still marked \"Revision history\" as *(stretch goal)*. | Marker removed now that it is built. Scheduled publishing keeps its marker until T16. |\n\n### Clarified: criterion 6 wording\n\nThe issue says \"a revision **id** belonging to a different item is refused\". The route identifies a revision by the item's own **version number** (`/admin/posts/{id}/revisions/{version}/rollback`). It looks that version up by `(content_id, kind, version)`. So another item's revision can't even be named; cross-item restore is impossible by construction. `test_a_version_of_a_different_item_cannot_be_rolled_back_to` covers both cases: a version that exists only on another Post, and a Page id used under `/admin/posts/`. The issue text has been updated to match.\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **No test that deleting an item deletes its revisions** (Spec). `delete_content` does delete them in the same transaction. But the only public read, `list_revisions`, joins `content`, so leftover rows would be invisible anyway, and `AUTOINCREMENT` never reuses an id. A test would have to query the table directly, a side channel this repo's tests avoid.\n- **The backfill credits the Author as who saved version 1** (Standards). The last editor was never stored before T15, so the Author is the best available answer. This is now said in the `BACKFILL_REVISIONS` comment.\n- **`connect()` both opens connections and brings the schema up to date** (Standards: possible Divergent Change). Kept: one guarded call per file per process is the simplest way to upgrade a student's existing `cms.db` with no new migration step or command. `Path.resolve()` on each connect costs microseconds.\n- **The rollback route repeats the \"load item → 303 → check CSRF → error\" opening of `update_item`** (Standards: Duplicated Code), and `title, slug, body_md` travel together (Data Clumps). Kept: the route follows the factory's existing pattern. Changing the shared shape would touch create/update/delete, which are outside this ticket.\n- **One more `saved == \"rolled-back\"` branch in `content_list.html`** (Repeated Switches). It follows the template's existing pattern.\n- **Small, harmless extras** (Spec, scope): a \"Post/Page rolled back.\" banner, a \"UTC\" suffix on revision times, and a `.badge--current` style.\n\n### Verification\n\n- Full suite: **233 passed** (221 before + 7 revision tests + 4 sweep cases + 1 failed-POST link case).\n- A copy of the real local `cms.db` (5 items, made before T15) opened cleanly. Each item got its version 1, with its Author and last-updated time.\n- The Revisions section was checked by screenshot at 1280px and 390px. Every admin screen still fits 390px, including the edit screens, which now list two revisions.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2060,"cache_read_input_tokens":141046,"output_tokens":2434,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2060,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2434,"cache_read_input_tokens":141046,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2060,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2060},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_015q3RbzzWqTkw7NLqWNZ8o1":{"file_path":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1\\scratchpad\\t15-review.md","content":"## /code-review findings — T15\n\nTwo independent reviewers read the diff fresh, in parallel. The **Standards** axis checked the CLAUDE.md rules, the CONTEXT.md vocabulary, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md and the Fowler smell baseline. The **Spec** axis mapped each acceptance criterion in this issue to the code and the tests.\n\n- **Hard rules are clean.** The Roll back form carries a `csrf_token`, and its action is relative (`{{ to_root }}…`). Revision titles and Markdown are autoescaped by Jinja. No new dependency was added. Drafts still never reach `site/`: export reads `content`, never `revisions`.\n- **Atomicity is clean.** The content row and its revision commit in one transaction. A duplicate-slug `IntegrityError` rolls both back.\n- **Spec:** every acceptance criterion is implemented. Six were fully covered by tests; the gaps the axis found were in assertions, not in behaviour (fixed below).\n\n### Fixed\n\n| # | Axis | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Standards | `_record_revision`'s docstring said \"Snapshot\", a word CONTEXT.md lists under *Avoid*. | It now says \"Record one save as the item's next Revision\". |\n| 2 | Standards | `update_content(..., editor_id=)` used a role name (Editor) for a value that can be an Admin. | Renamed to `saved_by`, matching the column. |\n| 3 | Standards | Comments said a Roll back \"restores\", and CONTEXT.md's own definition began with \"Restoring\", although it lists \"restore\" under *Avoid*. | Comments say \"rolls back to\" / \"returns to\"; the glossary now says \"Returning an item's title, slug, and body to those of an earlier Revision\". |\n| 4 | Standards | `db.connect()` leaked the connection if the schema upgrade raised, and leaked again on every later call. | The upgrade now lives in `init_db`, which closes its own connection in `finally`. `connect()` opens its connection only after that succeeds. The two-line `_upgrade` middle man is gone. |\n| 5 | Standards | `init_db` became a no-op for a database file already seen by the process. | `init_db` always runs the schema and backfill. Only `connect()` skips it once a file is known. |\n| 6 | Standards | `app/seed.py` inserts content directly, so seeded items got no version 1 until the next process start. If the server was already running, the seeded text was lost from history on the first edit. | `_seed_content` runs the backfill in the same transaction. New test `test_seeded_demo_content_starts_with_a_first_revision` fails without the fix and passes with it. |\n| 7 | Standards | The tests' `_create_post` took `list_content(...)[0]`, which ties on `created_at` (1-second resolution) when two posts are made in the same second. That could make tests flaky. | It looks the post up by its slug. |\n| 8 | Spec | Criterion 1: nothing asserted \"who and when\" beyond the email, or who saved a Roll back. | Asserts a `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC` timestamp, and that an Admin's Roll back of an Editor's post is recorded under the Admin. |\n| 9 | Spec | Criterion 2: nothing asserted that the Markdown is viewable, or that Roll back appears only on earlier versions. | Both are asserted. |\n| 10 | Spec | Criterion 4: the slug-conflict test didn't assert the status code. | Asserts 200 (the editor is re-rendered with the error). |\n| 11 | Spec | Criterion 9: a *failed* Roll back POST, which renders at the deeper `/revisions/1/rollback` URL, wasn't in the link-resolution test. | Added to `FAILED_POST_PAGES`. |\n| 12 | Standards | CONTEXT.md still marked \"Revision history\" as *(stretch goal)*. | Marker removed now that it is built. Scheduled publishing keeps its marker until T16. |\n\n### Clarified: criterion 6 wording\n\nThe issue says \"a revision **id** belonging to a different item is refused\". The route identifies a revision by the item's own **version number** (`/admin/posts/{id}/revisions/{version}/rollback`). It looks that version up by `(content_id, kind, version)`. So another item's revision can't even be named; cross-item restore is impossible by construction. `test_a_version_of_a_different_item_cannot_be_rolled_back_to` covers both cases: a version that exists only on another Post, and a Page id used under `/admin/posts/`. The issue text has been updated to match.\n\n### Deliberately not changed (judgement calls)\n\n- **No test that deleting an item deletes its revisions** (Spec). `delete_content` does delete them in the same transaction. But the only public read, `list_revisions`, joins `content`, so leftover rows would be invisible anyway, and `AUTOINCREMENT` never reuses an id. A test would have to query the table directly, a side channel this repo's tests avoid.\n- **The backfill credits the Author as who saved version 1** (Standards). {"parentUuid":"705a69e3-4177-4e3c-a7d5-2a4e9646b3f1","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1\\scratchpad\\t15-issue.md","snippet":"14\t\n15\t## Acceptance criteria\n16\t\n17\t- [ ] Creating, editing, and rolling back a Post or Page each record a revision with title, slug, body, who and when\n18\t- [ ] The edit screen lists revisions newest first, marks the current one, and offers Roll back on the others\n19\t- [ ] Rolling back restores the old title, slug and body and records a new revision noting the rollback\n20\t- [ ] Rolling back to a slug now used by another item of the same kind shows the editor's \"slug already used\" error and changes nothing\n21\t- [ ] Editors and Admins can roll back; anonymous visitors are redirected to log in\n22\t- [ ] Only the item's own versions can be rolled back to: a version number is looked up within that item, so no cross-item restore\n23\t- [ ] The rollback route rejects a forged CSRF token and is part of the access-control sweep\n24\t- [ ] A database created before this ticket gains the `revisions` table and a starting revision per existing item, with no re-seed\n25\t- [ ] The edit screen with revisions fits a 390px phone and every link on it stays relative and resolves\n26\t- [ ] `CONTEXT.md` defines Revision and Roll back\n27\t- [ ] The full test suite passes\n28\t\n29\t## Blocked by\n30\t"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"7399ddb2-25f0-45ba-b4b3-b49094c5f0bb","timestamp":"2026-10-07T05:35:26.506Z","rendered":[{"content":"<system-reminder>\nNote: C:\\Users\\rajan\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\C--Rajan-E-disk-My-work-IPHS400-code-mp2-cms\\79460543-7a02-4f77-9f1a-bef5b403f7a1\\scratchpad\\t15-issue.md changed on disk since you last read it. {"parentUuid":"a98571c7-9b47-47bc-93fe-2bb901a6e0d4","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfnLM99xYuVxpiUiVdd83","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T15 is ready to merge as **PR #17**. All 233 tests pass, and the review findings are posted on issue #16.\n\n**What the review found and how it's resolved:** the Standards and Spec reviewers raised 12 things I fixed, all in one batch. The ones that mattered most:\n- **Seeded demo content had no version 1.** Running the seed script while the app was already open meant the first edit lost the seeded text with no way back. Seeding now records version 1. I checked that the new test for this fails without the fix and passes with it.\n- **Two possible connection leaks** in the new database-upgrade code. Fixed.\n- **One test helper could pick the wrong post** when two posts were made in the same second. That could have made tests fail at random. Fixed.\n- **Wording:** a few comments used words `CONTEXT.md` says to avoid (\"snapshot\", \"restore\"), and the code said `editor_id` for a value that can belong to an Admin. Fixed, and the glossary wording was tidied to match.\n- **Weak tests:** several acceptance criteria had thin assertions. They're now tighter.\n\nThe judgement calls I left alone are listed with reasons in the comment. I also reworded criterion 6 on the issue: rollback uses a version number looked up within the same item, not a revision id.\n\n**Commit:** `1a513c0 T15: …`, which ends in `Closes #16`. The PR also includes your docs commit `d4d5b4a`, because `main` hadn't been pushed yet. Merging the PR puts both on `origin/main`, so nothing extra is needed.\n\n**Not committed:** `notes/usage-ledger.csv` and the session 06 and 07 transcripts. They're yours to commit.\n\n**Before merging, you could try it yourself:** run `cms serve`, open any post's edit screen, edit it, then roll it back. An `<input type=\"datetime-local\">` gives a naive local time. Decide whether to convert from the machine's local zone or label the input as UTC. Test the boundary with a fixed \"now\" (inject it); don't use the wall clock.\n4. **Revisions.** Under T15's rule, publish and unpublish record no Revision. Setting or clearing a schedule is status-like, so by the same logic it should record none. Add a Python step in `init_db` that checks `PRAGMA table_info(content)` and runs `ALTER TABLE content ADD COLUMN publish_at TEXT` only when the column is missing.\n- Test it the way `tests/test_revisions.py::test_a_database_from_before_revisions_gets_a_starting_revision` does: a hand-written old schema (`PRE_T15_SCHEMA`), then monkeypatch `settings.DATABASE_PATH`. A new nullable column needs no seed change.\n- Also check the student's real `cms.db` by copying it to the scratchpad first; never open the real file during development.
